verifications.note: Energy Transfer spokesperson quoted: projects including 'the company's $4.2 billion Rover natural gas pipeline in Ohio' were 'under construction or beginning construction, all of which have been successfully completed and are operating today.'
Page description: 'Rover Pipeline LLC is a medium-sized ... pipeline company operating from Ohio to Howell, Michigan ... it functions at full capacity' (current data page, accessed 2026-09-09).

resolutions.researcher_notes: Two independent sources agree the pipeline is operating: a 2019 Grist/HuffPost piece quotes Energy Transfer stating Rover was completed and is operating, and Rextag's current data page (accessed 2026-09-09) describes it as an operating pipeline running at full capacity. No source found suggesting any change of status since.

verifications.note: Describes Rover as a pipeline moving 'up to 3.25 billion cubic feet of natural gas per day.'
Calls Rover 'a 711-mile-long (1,144-km) interstate natural gas pipeline in Ohio.'

resolutions.researcher_notes: Both sources independently confirm Rover carries natural gas; matches recorded Fuel=Gas.

verifications.note: 'FERC to revoke the certificate issued to the company in February [2017] that allowed it to start building the 42-inch natural gas pipeline, which is not yet in operation' — construction underway as of May 2017.
'In April 2017, shortly after Rover began its HDD operation, a large inadvertent release ... reached the surface' — construction activity dated to 2017.

resolutions.researcher_notes: FERC certificate issued Feb 2017 and active construction (incl. the Tuscarawas River HDD crossing) underway by April/May 2017, matching recorded ConstructionYear=2017.

verifications.note: Rover Pipeline entry: 'Status: Phase 1A of the pipeline is in-service and construction has started on Phase II ... Completion: 4Q 2017.'
'The company's goal is to have the pipeline in service from its origins ... to Defiance, Ohio by July and the rest of it in service by November' (2017).

resolutions.researcher_notes: Both sources place initial in-service in 2017 (Phase 1A in service with completion targeted 4Q2017 per Pipeline News; original July/November 2017 in-service target per Livingston Daily), matching recorded StartYear1=2017. Note full multi-lateral completion slipped into 2018 (see Reuters $40M penalty piece / roverpipelinefacts.com Nov 2018 lateral announcement in seed_citations) — StartYearEarliest=2017 is still correct as the earliest in-service date.

Searched Pipeline News PN1018 (s3.amazonaws.com PDF), PBS NewsHour, Livingston Daily, DeSmog, Reuters ($40M penalty piece), Grist/HuffPost, and Rextag. Every source that states a capacity figure gives the FULL system design capacity as 3.25 Bcf/d (PN1018: 'Capacity: 3.25 Bcf/d'; PBS: 'up to 3.25 billion cubic feet of natural gas per day') — none states 1,700 MMcf/d (1.7 Bcf/d) for any named 'Phase 1' sub-component. CONTRADICTS the sheet: recorded Capacity=1700 MMcf/d does not match any capacity figure found in independent sourcing for this pipeline; 1,700 MMcf/d is roughly half of the well-documented 3.25 Bcf/d full-system capacity, suggesting the recorded value may reflect only one of the two parallel mainlines (A/B) or a stale/partial pre-completion estimate that current public sources no longer carry. Flagging for orchestrator review rather than forcing a REFS_ADDED against a value no source actually states.

verifications.note: '...construction of a 711-mile-long (1,144-km) interstate natural gas pipeline in Ohio.' Exact match to recorded LengthKnown=711 mi / LengthKnownKm=1144.24.
Rover Pipeline entry: 'Length: 713 miles' — within rounding of the recorded 711 mi (2-mile/0.3% gap).

resolutions.researcher_notes: Reuters states the exact recorded figure (711 mi / 1,144 km). Pipeline News gives 713 mi, a 2-mile rounding-level discrepancy consistent with different as-built vs. certificated mileage; noted but not material. Livingston Daily (2017, pre-construction) additionally gives 710 mi, same rounding band, reinforcing 711 as correct.

verifications.note: '...allowed it to start building the 42-inch natural gas pipeline...' — exact match to recorded Diameter=42in.
Rover Pipeline entry: 'Diameter: 24, 30, 36 and 42 inches' — 42in is the primary mainline diameter listed among the sizes used across the system.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Livingston Daily names 42-inch as THE pipeline's diameter (mainline). Pipeline News lists the fuller size range used across mainlines/laterals (24-42in), consistent with 42in as the recorded primary/mainline diameter.

'...will transport natural gas from fracking operations in the Appalachian region of eastern Ohio, western Pennsylvania and northern West Virginia' — corroborates Marcellus/Utica Appalachian supply basin.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Rextag states the exact recorded phrase 'Marcellus and Utica Shale.' Livingston Daily independently corroborates the Appalachian shale-gas supply basin.

verifications.note: Rover Pipeline entry: 'Location: Ashland, OH - Howell, MI' — exact match to recorded Start=Ohio, End=Michigan.
'...origins in southeastern Ohio ... to Defiance, Ohio ... will pass through Lenawee, Washtenaw and Livingston counties in Michigan' — corroborates Ohio origin, Michigan terminus.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Both sources place the route as originating in Ohio and terminating in Michigan, matching recorded StartState=Ohio/EndState=Michigan (both US). Livingston Daily additionally notes the route also touches West Virginia and Pennsylvania between the recorded endpoints, consistent with GEM's segment-level Start/End simplification.

Searched Pipeline News PN1018, PBS NewsHour, Livingston Daily, Grist/HuffPost, DeSmog, Reuters, and Rextag. Every source that states a project cost gives a full-system figure in the $4.2-4.3 billion range (PN1018: 'Cost: $4.2 billion'; PBS: '$4.2 billion project'; Livingston Daily, 2017 pre-construction estimate: 'The $4.3 billion Rover Pipeline project'; Grist/HuffPost: "the company's $4.2 billion Rover natural gas pipeline"). None states $3,000,000,000 for any 'Phase 1' sub-component. CONTRADICTS the sheet: recorded SegmentCost=$3,000,000,000 does not match any cost figure found in four independent, mutually-corroborating sources for the same pipeline. Flagging for orchestrator review rather than forcing a REFS_ADDED against a value no source actually states.
